films.title: Clay Box
films.description: Clay Howell's 17-minute independent film builds a handmade world around 24 documented skaters, shifting between street footage, three pool passages, Super 8 textures, animation and claymation. Its coast-to-coast spot record includes San Francisco's China Banks and New York's Brooklyn Banks.
creditNotes: Clay Howell's own channel publishes the uninterrupted complete film under his name and reports a March 4, 2026 publication date, 1,046-second runtime and permitted external embed.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies Clay Box as a 17-minute 2026 independent film by Clay Howell and catalogs all 24 skating appearances plus five production contributors.

The source does not assign named solo parts, so the complete roster is retained as documented appearances rather than promoting riders to unsupported part status. The five additional contributors retain SkateVideoSite's generic production-credit label.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite identifies the United States as the production country and specifically documents China Banks in San Francisco and Brooklyn Banks in New York City.
films.historicalContext: Clay Box is a 2026 independent release whose handmade visual identity extends from clay lettering and box artwork into documented claymation and animation, while its Super 8 and pool-skating sections connect the project to older skate-film textures.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is dedicated handmade CLAY BOX title art using clay letters and a caution-tape box, with no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

films.title: CACHÉ
films.description: Ryan Urie-Buxton's 17-minute Toronto film gives full parts to Justin Behan, Cody French, Urie-Buxton and François Héroux, surrounded by four city montages and 20 additional documented appearances. Shot on a Sony VX1000, it keeps filming, editing, titles and animation in Urie-Buxton's hands while crediting seven additional camera contributors.
creditNotes: The filmmaker's complete-film description formally identifies the four full parts, Ryan Urie-Buxton's filming, editing, titles and animation roles, all seven additional filmers and the Sony VX1000 camera.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies CACHÉ as a 17-minute 2026 Toronto independent film, corroborates the four full parts and seven production contributors, and catalogs all 24 appearances.
Only the four riders formally billed with full parts are labeled that way; the remaining independently documented skaters are retained as montage appearances.
films.locationNote: The authorized title identifies Toronto skateboarding, while SkateVideoSite independently records Toronto and the CBC Toronto spot.
films.historicalContext: CACHÉ is a contemporary Toronto independent film built around the Sony VX1000 visual language, pairing four named full parts with a broad local montage roster and filmmaker-made titles and animation.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's available YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It shows a fisheye Toronto street-skating frame with the CACHÉ title and no trailer, episode or compilation labeling; YouTube does not expose a max-resolution thumbnail for this upload, so the live hqdefault asset is retained.

films.title: Into The Void
films.description: Dan Rusin's 16-minute Surveillance Society of Minnesota film centers full sections on TJ Moran and Matt Boeltl, with Mirza Jasarovic, Mikee Carter and Josiah Clarke also formally featured. A deep 21-skater Midwest roster, Super 8 texture and documented Minneapolis and Boston spots expand the project beyond its five headline riders.
creditNotes: Village Psychic's complete-film description presents the project as a Surveillance Society of Minnesota commission, names TJ Moran and Matt Boeltl with Mirza Jasarovic, Mikee Carter and Josiah Clarke, and formally credits Dan Rusin with filming and editing.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies Into The Void as a 16-minute 2026 Dan Rusin film, catalogs all 21 appearances and Cam Herman's production credit, and preserves the section-level soundtrack structure.

TJ Moran and Matt Boeltl receive individually named soundtrack sections. Mirza Jasarovic, Mikee Carter and Josiah Clarke are retained as formally featured riders; the remaining documented skaters are separated as montage or additional appearances.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite documents Minneapolis as the primary location, Eggs in Boston as a filmed spot and the film's wider Midwest identity.
films.historicalContext: Commissioned by the Surveillance Society of Minnesota and released in both DVD and paid digital editions, Into The Void extends Dan Rusin's long-running record of Minnesota skateboarding through a compact contemporary film with Super 8 texture and a broad regional cast.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is dedicated title artwork reading INTO THE VOID and 'Produced by the Surveillance Society of Minnesota,' with no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.
